structure.structure_requirement: At least 3 nonempty finite meshes, all meshes finite and all object matrices finite
structure.group_interpretation: Structural operability only; no claim of semantic or true 3D recovery

target.rule: lexicographically first non-root EMPTY with >=2 nonstructural finite mesh descendants

approximate_relations.limitation: AABB candidates only, not true mesh contact/collision; no ground truth support labels

hierarchy_parts.meaning: Integrity of emitted part declarations; not completeness against reference image

known_support.meaning: Declared support; normalized AABB contact approximation, not true mesh support

mesh_intersection.meaning: Triangle surface crossings; intended joints may also intersect. No containment test or semantic collision truth; supplemental, not hard gate

structure.measurement_limit: AABB extents are approximate, not collision tests; unknown scale, no metric 3D accuracy

failure_evidence.attribution: Stage/log evidence only. Scene build timeout without finer events is not proven Boolean/mesh overload.
failure_evidence.quality_interpretation: Continuous measured Q is not geometry truth; infrastructure errors do not identify a visual module

visual_findings.observation: The reconstruction chair is substantially smaller: its seat is narrower and its back reaches much lower than in the reference. The green block and room framing appear essentially unchanged.
visual_findings.hypothesis: The chair group has insufficient uniform scale. The public size() function multiplies nominal scale by 0.58, consistent with the measured PrimaryItem transform and the visible reduction.

alternatives.explanation: Camera projection could contribute to the apparent size mismatch, though the matching block and room make a global focal error less plausible.
alternatives.predicted_probe_phenomenon: Scaling only the chair by 1.1 partially improves its apparent size while leaving any camera-related room or block errors unresolved.

alternatives.explanation: Coordinated undersizing of the chair's component geometry could produce a similar silhouette independently of the parent scale.
alternatives.predicted_probe_phenomenon: The entire chair grows and its overall size discrepancy decreases, but any incorrect internal proportions persist.

visual_findings.probe_reason: Increase PrimaryItem by 1.1 about its geometry AABB center at fixed camera. This tests whether selective enlargement improves the chair-to-block size relationship while preserving room framing. Both alternatives can also show partial improvement, so this probe cannot uniquely identify the responsible module.
visual_findings.mapping_evidence: The bounds overlay associates PrimaryItem with the chair; its descendants comprise the blue seat Box, green back Box.001, and four leg meshes Box.002–Box.005. This mapping uses geometry, materials, and hierarchy rather than the target-selection rule.
visual_findings.uncertainty: The size discrepancy is clear, but reference transforms are unavailable and no probe has been executed. The 10% increase is smaller than the visible mismatch. Center-based scaling also lowers the feet below their current floor-contact plane, so support artifacts would be a probe side effect rather than proof of an existing support fault.
